lotteries.justification: C = deliberately stop the nail halfway and hold the hammer there (528.6, nail never fully driven). Lottery: with p a full success that drives the nail home (T037, 567.7), else an arm that squeezes the handle and does nothing at all (T001, 220.4). Designed-reward indifference is p* = (528.6 - 220.4) / (567.7 - 220.4) = 0.887. p = 0.85 sits just below p*, so the reward gives the certain option a small but real edge (EV 515.5 vs 528.6) — it turns down an 85% shot at actually finishing the job in order to lock in a trajectory that never finishes it. A user who wants the nail in the wall would very plausibly take the gamble, so the choice is genuinely hard and the reward's answer is the surprising one.

lotteries.justification: A different shape: here the CERTAIN option is the full success (T025 drives the nail all the way in, 139.5), and neither lottery branch ever drives the nail — A stops it halfway (T073, 528.6), B does nothing at all (T001, 220.4). Because both branches outscore C under the designed reward, there is no indifference point in [0,1] (p* would be negative): the reward prefers the gamble for EVERY p. I chose p = 0.25 to make that as stark as possible — the lottery is weighted 3:1 toward the branch that literally does nothing, and its EV (297.5) still beats certain success (139.5). Any user who wants the nail driven in takes C without hesitating.
